title: MedicationSafetyAllergyTaxonomy
description: Comprehensive Clinical Allergy Taxonomy and Cross-Referencing Knowledge Base for Active Ingredients and Inactive Excipients in Pharmaceutical Products.

metadata_schema.description: Standard User Entry Metadata Schema for patient-reported or clinician-verified allergy profiles

allergy_id.description: Unique identifier for the patient's allergy record

trigger_name.description: Name of the drug, drug class, food allergen, or excipient (e.g., Amoxicillin, Penicillins, Lactose Monohydrate, Gelatin, Latex)

reaction_type.description: Immunologic classification of the adverse response

symptoms.description: Array of clinical symptoms (e.g., Urticaria, Angioedema, Bronchospasm, Hypotension, Maculopapular Rash, Dyspepsia, Headache)

notes.description: Clinical context, date of onset, or diagnostic test details (skin prick, specific IgE)

cross_reactive_classes.mechanism: Beta-lactam ring core plus R1 side-chain similarity. 1st-generation cephalosporins (Cephalexin, Cefadroxil, Cefazolin) share high R1 similarity with ampicillin/amoxicillin (~5-10% cross-reactivity). 3rd/4th/5th-gen (Ceftriaxone, Cefepime) have distinct side-chains (<1% cross-reactivity unless side chains match).
Bicyclic beta-lactam core cross-reactivity historically cited as 50%, modern clinical evidence demonstrates <1% cross-reactivity in proven IgE-mediated penicillin allergy.
Monocyclic beta-lactam ring does not cross-react with penicillins, EXCEPT Ceftazidime (shares identical R1 side chain with Aztreonam).

cross_reactive_classes.rule: Flag exact R1/R2 side chain match as Critical. Flag discordant side chain generations as Caution.

antibiotic_arylamines.description: Contain N4 aromatic amine substituent directly attached to benzene ring linked to sulfonamide group (N1). Primary driver of severe IgE and T-cell mediated reactions (SJS/TEN).

non_antibiotic_sulfonamides.description: Lack the N4 arylamine moiety. Cross-reactivity with antibiotic sulfas is immunologically minimal to nonexistent, but cautious clinical awareness is warranted.

cross_reactive_classes.mechanism: Large macrocyclic lactone ring shared across members.
Common bicyclic core structure; high rates of IgE cross-sensitization.

vancomycin.differentiating_note: Rapid infusion causes non-IgE mast cell degranulation (Red Man Syndrome); rate reduction mitigates response. True IgE requires desensitization.

aerd_cross_reactive.name: Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease / Cross-Reactive Urticaria
aerd_cross_reactive.mechanism: Non-allergic pseudoallergy driven by COX-1 inhibition shifting arachidonic acid cascade to overproduction of cysteinyl leukotrienes.
safe_alternatives: Celecoxib (selective COX-2 inhibitor, highly tolerated in AERD)

single_nsaid_ige_allergy.name: Single Drug IgE-Mediated Hypersensitivity
single_nsaid_ige_allergy.mechanism: Immunologic IgE specific to single chemical structure (e.g., Ibuprofen IgE may tolerate Diclofenac or Naproxen).

phenanthrenes.note: Most prone to non-immunologic direct mast cell degranulation causing flushing/pruritus. Cross-reactivity within phenanthrenes is high.

phenylpiperidines.note: Distinct structure; rarely causes direct histamine release. Safe choice in phenanthrene allergy.

diphenylheptanes.note: Structurally distinct third class for true opioid allergy substitution.

acetaminophen.reaction_profile: Hypersensitivity is rare. Doses > 1000mg may weakly inhibit COX-1 and trigger mild bronchospasm in 25% of severe AERD patients.

esters.cross_reactivity: High cross-reactivity within ester group due to PABA. Also cross-reacts with methylparaben preservative in multidose vials.

amides.cross_reactivity: Virtually zero cross-reactivity between Esters and Amides. Amide-to-amide cross-reactivity is extremely rare. True allergy is <1%; most reactions are vasovagal or epinephrine-related.

propofol.vehicle: Oil-in-water lipid emulsion containing 10% soybean oil and 1.2% purified egg phosphatide (egg lecithin).
propofol.clinical_guidance: AAAI guidelines note egg phosphatide is purified from yolk (not egg white ovalbumin); true reactions in egg-allergic patients are exceedingly rare. Soybean oil is refined and devoid of protein. Flag as Tier 3 Caution, not Hard Stop.

neuromuscular_blocking_agents.mechanism: Quaternary ammonium ion epitopes. Cross-reactivity between different NMBAs ranges between 60% and 80%.

ace_inhibitors.contraindication_rule: Angioedema to one ACE inhibitor is an ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to ALL other ACE inhibitors. ARBs (Losartan, Valsartan) carry ~2-7% theoretical cross-over risk.

iodinated_contrast_media.reaction: Non-allergic chemotoxic or anaphylactoid (direct complement/mast cell) reaction.
iodinated_contrast_media.clinical_myth_rule: DEBUNKED: Seafood/shellfish allergy is caused by tropomyosin protein, NOT iodine. Shellfish allergy does NOT increase ICM reaction risk more than any general atopic condition.

chimeric_murine.risk: Contains human/mouse chimeric sequences. Cetuximab contains alpha-gal epitope.

fully_human.risk: 100% human sequence; lowest anti-drug antibody formation.

egg_protein_content.yellow_fever_vaccine: High ovalbumin content; requires skin testing/specialist desensitization in severe egg allergy.
egg_protein_content.influenza_vaccines: Current CDC/ACIP guidelines state egg-allergic individuals may receive any licensed, age-appropriate flu vaccine without special precautions.

gelatin_stabilizer.risk: Porcine gelatin stabilizer can trigger severe anaphylaxis in gelatin-sensitized or Alpha-gal patients.

pharmaceutical_excipients.usage: Filler/binder in tablets and carrier in Dry Powder Inhalers (DPIs e.g. Fluticasone/Salmeterol Diskus).
pharmaceutical_excipients.clinical_significance: Pharmaceutical-grade lactose may contain trace milk proteins. While tolerated by lactose intolerant patients, DPI inhalation in severe milk IgE anaphylaxis has caused fatal bronchospasm.

pharmaceutical_excipients.usage: Solvent/vehicle in sustained-release intramuscular injections (Testosterone cypionate/enanthate, Haloperidol decanoate, Progesterone, Fluphenazine).
pharmaceutical_excipients.clinical_significance: Pure sesame allergy can trigger systemic anaphylaxis upon IM injection of sesame oil depot.

pharmaceutical_excipients.usage: Capsule solvent (Prometrium / Progesterone capsules), Dimercaprol injections, topical emollients.
pharmaceutical_excipients.clinical_significance: Refined peanut oil has reduced protein, but FDA mandates contraindication on Prometrium for peanut-allergic individuals.

pharmaceutical_excipients.usage: Lipid vehicle in Propofol emulsions, Clevidipine (Cleviprex), Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN/Intralipid).
pharmaceutical_excipients.clinical_significance: Highly refined oil has low antigenic protein; extreme IgE cases warrant cautious evaluation.

pharmaceutical_excipients.usage: Topical dermatologics, ear drops, lipophilic bases.
pharmaceutical_excipients.clinical_significance: Risk of cutaneous and mucosal absorption triggering contact dermatitis or systemic symptoms.

pharmaceutical_excipients.usage: Emulsifying agent in Propofol, Clevidipine, and TPN lipid emulsions.
pharmaceutical_excipients.clinical_significance: Derived from yolk; generally low in ovomucoid/white allergen, but FDA prescribing information notes contraindication for severe egg allergy.

pharmaceutical_excipients.usage: Antibacterial preservative in troches, lozenges, and topical ophthalmics.

pharmaceutical_excipients.clinical_significance: Contains residual gliadin/gluten (<100 ppm). Critical for Celiac Disease patients and IgE wheat-allergic patients.

pharmaceutical_excipients.usage: Most widely used tablet filler and disintegrant; safe for gluten-sensitive patients.
Over-the-counter joint supplement synthesized from chitin of shrimp/crab shells.
pharmaceutical_excipients.clinical_significance: Shellfish IgE allergy is to muscle protein (tropomyosin), not chitin; however, cross-contamination with flesh protein during processing can occur. Non-shellfish synthetic/vegetarian forms exist.

pharmaceutical_excipients.usage: Heparin reversal agent and NPH insulin component.
pharmaceutical_excipients.clinical_significance: Derived from salmon or other fish sperm. Significant anaphylaxis risk in individuals with severe fish allergy or previous vasectomy.

pharmaceutical_excipients.excipient_name: Cod Liver Oil / Omega-3 Fatty Acids
pharmaceutical_excipients.usage: Fish oil capsules (Lovaza, Vascepa); highly purified ethyl esters, but contraindicated in severe fish anaphylaxis.

gelatin.clinical_significance: Strong IgE reactivity; pivotal trigger in patients with Alpha-gal syndrome (mammalian carbohydrate allergy) who cannot tolerate porcine/bovine gelatin.

alpha_gal_syndrome.mechanism: Carbohydrate epitope transferred via Lone Star tick (Amblyomma americanum) bites, sensitizing IgE to mammalian meat and products.
pharmaceutical_threats: Cetuximab (contains alpha-gal on murine Fab portion -> fatal first-dose anaphylaxis)
Porcine Heparin and Enoxaparin (low molecular weight heparins)
Gelatin-based capsules and intravenous colloid plasma volume expanders (Gelofusine)

stearates.source: May be derived from bovine tallow or plant/vegetable oils. Vegetarian formulations avoid animal stearate.

tartrazine_fdc_yellow_5.usage: Widely used yellow pigment in coated tablets, syrups, and vitamin preparations.
tartrazine_fdc_yellow_5.clinical_significance: Known to cause urticaria, angioedema, and bronchospasm in 10-15% of aspirin-sensitive (AERD) patients due to shared inflammatory mediator pathways.

fdc_red_40_allura_red.usage: Pediatric liquid medications, suspension flavor colorings.

carmine_cochineal_natural_red_4.usage: Natural red dye derived from crushed female Dactylopius coccus insects.
carmine_cochineal_natural_red_4.clinical_significance: Direct protein-mediated IgE anaphylaxis documented in allergic patients.

sulfites.usage: Antioxidant in injectable Epinephrine (EpiPen), local anesthetics containing epinephrine, dexamethasone injections, and topical eye drops.
sulfites.clinical_significance: Induces severe steroid-dependent bronchospasm in asthmatics. Note: Epinephrine must NEVER be withheld during anaphylaxis regardless of sulfite content.

parabens.usage: Antimicrobial preservative in multidose vials (multidose local anesthetics, heparin, bacteriostatic saline), creams, and cosmetics.
parabens.clinical_significance: Ester of PABA. Responsible for pseudo-local anesthetic allergies (reactions to multidose lidocaine are often paraben reactions).

benzyl_alcohol.usage: Bacteriostatic preservative in multidose injectable solutions and heparin flush.
benzyl_alcohol.clinical_significance: Contraindicated in neonates and low-birth-weight infants due to toxic 'gasping syndrome', metabolic acidosis, and CNS depression.

propylene_glycol.usage: Solvent for poorly soluble IV drugs (Lorazepam, Diazepam, Phenytoin, Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole).
propylene_glycol.clinical_significance: High-dose continuous IV infusions cause severe hyperosmolality, lactic acidosis, acute kidney injury, and contact hypersensitivity.

benzalkonium_chloride_bak.clinical_significance: Causes corneal epithelial toxicity, blepharoconjunctivitis, and paradoxical bronchoconstriction in nebulizer solutions.

polyethylene_glycol_peg.usage: Bowel cleansing solutions (MiraLAX, GoLYTELY), mRNA COVID-19 vaccine lipid nanoparticles, drug pegylation.

polysorbate_80_and_20.usage: Non-ionic surfactants in biologic infusions (Monoclonal antibodies, Darbepoetin, Intravenous Amiodarone).
polysorbate_80_and_20.cross_reactivity: High cross-reactivity between PEG and Polysorbate due to shared polymerized ethylene oxide moieties.

aspartame.usage: Artificial sweetener in chewable tablets, orally disintegrating tablets (ODTs), and pediatric liquids.
aspartame.clinical_significance: Metabolized to phenylalanine. ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION for patients with Phenylketonuria (PKU).

sorbitol_and_mannitol.usage: Osmotic fillers in chewable tablets and sugar-free syrups. May cause osmotic diarrhea, bloating, and abdominal cramping at high cumulative daily doses.

latex_fruit_syndrome.mechanism: Class I chitinases with hevein-like domains cross-react with Hev b 6.02 latex major allergen in 30-50% of latex-allergic patients.

natural_rubber_latex.screening_rule: Flag any injectable or transdermal product whose package insert does not state 'Not Made with Natural Rubber Latex'.

acrylates.usage: Continuous glucose monitor (CGM) adhesives, insulin pump infusion sets, transdermal drug delivery patches (Fentanyl, Clonidine, Nicotine).
acrylates.clinical_significance: Causes severe allergic contact dermatitis and blistering.

colophony_rosin.usage: Tackifying agent in adhesive surgical tapes, wound dressings, and topical ointments.

nickel.risk: Contact hypersensitivity from dental appliances, surgical staples, cardiac occluder devices.
